correctness.rationale: The centered parallelotope has inradius half the minimum generator-to-opposite-face altitude. The Gram formula 2R=sqrt(Delta/(1-min(a^2,b^2,c^2))) follows by three cofactor identities, and independent spherical polar angles give density (4pi sqrt Delta)^(-1). R>1/2-epsilon forces each correlation to O(sqrt epsilon). On scaling by 2 sqrt epsilon, the event converges to the tricylinder with negligible boundary and bounded support, so dominated convergence yields a sharp coefficient (8/(4pi))*8(2-sqrt2)=16(2-sqrt2)/pi and L1/total-variation convergence of conditional densities. Wedge integration exactly evaluates the cylinder volume and homogeneity yields the Beta(3/2,1) deficit. 2,000 direct facet tests and a 1,500,000-sample seeded check passed; these are only corroborative.

value.rationale: The inradius of a random three-generator parallelotope is its natural worst-face clearance, a robustness observable not determined by its volume; the differing-inradius equal-determinant example proves this distinction. The precise 3/2 rare-event exponent and explicit 16(2-sqrt2)/pi coefficient connect this natural problem to a nonellipsoidal tricylinder, while the total-variation conditional geometry and exact Beta deficit describe the entire first-order shape fluctuation. This is a mathematically motivated exact geometric distribution statement, not a renamed determinant moment, arbitrary parameter slice, or known table recomputation. The classical tricylinder volume is a credited ingredient.
